textbookText: 15.1 Introduction Refraction of light is the fundamental concept in the field of optics which unveils the behavior of light as it travels through different media. Refraction of light, bending of light rays as they pass from one medium to another, plays a vital role in twinkling of stars in the night sky, bending of straw in a glass of water, shimmering of a mirage in a desert. ThesStudy of this fundamental phenomenon, refraction, provides a better understanding of the principles involved in the above mentioned phenomena and the mysteries behind them. Also, the study of refraction provides the foundation for the design of optical lenses, prisms, optical pipes, optical fibers and many more. This chapter provides a clear picture of the refraction of light and its influencing behaviors on our world.
15.2 Refraction of light

When a ray of light travels from one medium to another it encounters a change in density. As a result, the velocity of light changes, and light suffers change in initial direction in the second medium. This phenomenon is called refraction of light. Hence, refraction is the phenomenon of bending of light as it goes obliquely from one medium to another.

When light encounters change in density of medium, it also suffers a change in velocity. The
change in velocity results in the change of direction of light. This change in direction of light
as it passes through a medium of varying density is called the refraction of light.

15.3 Laws of Refraction of Light
1. The incident ray, refracted ray, and normal at the point of the incident, all lie in the same
plane.
2. When light travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium, it bends toward the normal,
and when light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium; it bends away from the
normal.
3. For a given pair media, the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence (sini) to the sine of the
angle of refraction (sinr) is constant. The constant is called refractive index of the second
sini medium with respect to the first medium i.e. 12 =sinr . This is Snell’s law.
15.4 Refractive Index
Refractive index is the fundamental physical property that describes how light propagates
through a material. It indicates the speed at which light travels through a particular material
relative to the speed of light in a vacuum. For example, the refractive index of water is
approximately 1.33 which means that the speed of light in water is about 75% of the speed
of light in a vacuum. The materials with higher refractive index are considered more
optically dense as they can slow down the propagation of light more than materials with
lower refractive index. The refractive index is denoted by  t is a dimensionless quantity.
